strategy.title: No plan: the only opening needs 48 owner hours of on-site teaching against a 20-hour allowance
strategy.why: The only held opening is the owner teaching eight-session lunchtime yoga programmes herself: $960 per programme (four signed), 12 owner hours each with no substitute instructor. $3,000 needs four programmes = 48 owner hours, against 4 h/week x 5 weeks = 20 owner hours; inside 20 hours only one programme ($960) fits. It is also the owner's own on-site physical work. No other opening is held.

alternatives.why: Rejected: 48 owner hours against a 20-hour window allowance, and the owner teaches on site personally.

alternatives.title: Run one programme inside the hours
alternatives.why: Rejected: 12 owner hours fit, but $960 is far short of the $3,000 target.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is right, and the gap it names is a true constraint rather than missing evidence: even with every fact established, the only held opening cannot fit the owner-hours limit. Each programme is 12 owner hours (eight 1.5 h sessions taught by the owner, no substitute engaged) at $960; three programmes give $2,880 < $3,000, so four are needed = 48 h against 4 h/week x 5 weeks = 20 h. Per week it is worse: each programme runs twice weekly (3 h/week), so four in parallel need ~12 h/week against 4. The OWNER_HOURS constraint is cited to the card's captureMechanism and price, and no unknown is treated as known.
findings: Recomputed: ceil(3000/960) = 4 programmes; 4 x $960 = $3,840; 4 x 12 h = 48 h > 20 h; one programme (3 h/week, $960, paid ~7 days after its last session ~day 30) is the most that fits.
Constraint OWNER_HOURS with basis captureMechanism + price is correct; decisiveLinks is empty, which is consistent with a limit-driven no-plan (no chain link is unestablished on the evidence).
Brain's exclusion also cites 'the owner does no physical work', while the contract records ownerPhysicalWork as UNSTATED; the hours constraint alone decides, so this does not change the verdict.

Brain's 69.7% figure comes from constructed estimates (coverage of assumed inputs, flagged implausible), not held openings; the revision correctly does not adopt it and directs research to openings fulfilled without the owner.
